KFNFH Hatchery Data Objects

Exploration, QC checks, object descriptions and a draft data dictionary

Purpose

The hatchery data objects of the package are built in data-raw/processing-scripts/process-hatchery-data.R and saved to data/. This document does not build anything: it loads the saved objects and explores them (a glimpse() and summaries of each), runs QC checks and plots on each one, describes each object, and holds a draft data dictionary.

Where values come from. Every value is taken from the annual reports (PDF text and tables) or the hatchery Excel workbooks. The one hand-compiled file the script reads is data-raw/hatchery-resources/mortality_events.csv, for the descriptive text of events E01-E28 (cause, location, population), which exists only as the a reading of the report narratives (the file records no author); every number in the events comes from the reports or workbooks.

How the objects are built. process-hatchery-data.R has these sections:

Part of the script What it does
PARSE PDF FILES, PROCESS TABLES Report tables of each year (FY2021-FY2025, cached in data-raw/pdf-tables/) into per-year objects; intermediate objects hatchery_release_2021_2024, adult_collection_2023_2024, pond_growout_reports_2021_2024, pen_survival_reports_2024
2. INPUTS FROM THE EXCEL WORKBOOKS AND THE REPORTS Reads the workbooks and report text/tables: mortality spreadsheets, production harvest, spawning crosses, broodstock, the age/facility lookup, collections and releases, capacity, and the mortality events (description, phrase in the report, loss and severity tier).
3. FINAL OBJECTS Merges the FY2021-2024 tables with FY2025 and the workbook inputs and saves the objects: lookup, collection and release history, pond grow-out, incubation and hatch, adult collection, hatchery release, net pens, early rearing, mortality events (E01-E37), monthly pond mortality, capacity, broodstock spawned.

Assumptions and decisions

Every number in the objects comes from the annual reports or the hatchery workbooks. The items below are the places where a rule, a reading of the text, or a choice between sources decides a value. They were made while building the objects, and each one should be confirmed or changed.

Area What was assumed or decided
Mortality events E01-E28: descriptions Which events exist, their category, mortality_event (yes/no), cause, location, affected population, loss_as_reported and confidence are a reading of the FY2021-2024 narratives, taken as written from the file mortality_events.csv (the file records no author). Each event is tied to a phrase in the report, but the reading itself is not checked against a table.
Mortality events: losses typed from the text E03 and E04 are 100% (“all perished”, “total losses within days of hatch”). E26 and E27 are 0% (no sucker mortality observed or attributed). E14 is 100 minus the 86% survival of the RZB fingerlings in the diet trial (Table 14), taking the trial survival as the event’s loss. E07 has no percent_lost: the report only says the Gerber net pen was emergency-harvested and 2,175 fish were moved, so no loss is stated; with no percent and mortality_event = no, its tier is “Non-mortality”.
Mortality events: severity tier Over 70% is Catastrophic, 30-70% Major, 10-30% Moderate, under 10% Minor; an event that is not a mortality event is “Near-miss” if its loss is 0 and “Non-mortality” otherwise; an event with no percent is “Qualitative only”. These thresholds follow the tier labels in mortality_events.csv, not a report.
Mortality events: fish lost (n_mortality) Filled for E01, E11, E12 and E16 among E01-E28 (where the reports give the fish lost); counts that could be computed for others (for example E08, E17, E19) are left NA. For E29-E37 it is filled whenever a count exists.
FY2025 events E29-E37 The category, mortality_event and confidence labels and the wording of the description columns are mine, written from the FY2025 report. E29: the loss is the fish at the start minus (harvested + harvest-day deaths), the definition of the Survival column of Sheet1, and Sheet1 is used rather than the Production Harvest workbook (they disagree on the harvested fish). E33: “just under 70% survival” is taken to be the P10 cycle in the Production Harvest workbook (sheet Spring 2025). E34: the event window runs from the first July day with 10 or more dead fish to the last day the staff note stratification; the loss is recorded deaths only, over the fish at the start in the Production Harvest workbook (sheet Fall 2025). E35: uses the Table 8 total of 3,562 deaths, not the 3,652 in the report text. E30, E32, E37: no number of fish at risk is given, so there is no percent.
Pond grow-out A completed cycle listed in two reports is kept once (the later report’s row, 44 cycles); a cycle reported in progress is replaced by its completed record; fiscal_year is the year of the report that lists the cycle; numeric pond IDs (“0”) become “P0”; weight_gain_lb merges a misspelled duplicate column; life_history is “ESS” when the lot name contains “ESS”; the FY2025 report tables are read by column position, with months and growth split from one text cell.
Age lookup All built by rules: net pens age = operation year minus capture year; ponds age class = fiscal year minus the lot’s collection year (4 means 4 or older), East Side Springs and mixed lots “other”, wild or salvage lots “wild”; a cycle counts in the fiscal year it was stocked and in the fiscal year it was harvested; starting_count is the fish at the start of the first cycle harvested in the year.
Capacity The pond counts and sizes are typed from report sentences, and each sentence is checked against the report text. FY2024 is set to 22 ponds because the four A-series ponds were demolished early in the year. The FY2022 report says “nearly 2.1 acres” but its own pond counts give 2.38 acres, and 2.38 is used. The planned row’s year (2028) is an assumption: the FY2025 report only says the build-out is “beyond 2027/2028”. Indoor gallons are summed from the tank lists by text pattern, counting each research rack sump (4 x 180 gallons) as capacity.
Rounding total_eggs is rounded to whole numbers, hatch_percent to one decimal (and captive eggs_per_mL to two), as in Excel, so FY2025 incubation values differ slightly from the raw workbook values (for example 3,255.78 is 3,256).
Incubation and adult collection FY2024 family_groups is the number of males listed (the table has no such value). Short PIT tags (4-5 characters) are expanded to the full tag when exactly one tag in the FY2025 workbook or report table ends with them. Adult sex M/F is recoded to Male/Female.
Collection and release history larvae_collected is taken from Table 7 (30,150 for FY2024) rather than Table 1 (30,142); total_released is the sum of the four release columns; broodstock_on_station is the number parsed from “approximately” or “over” in the report text; FY2021 new_broodstock_reported (300) is read from “300 broodstock selected”.
Early rearing restock is set from the word “Restock” in the culture-unit name; date is the first date when a row lists two days.
QC checks The tolerances (for example 5% for eggs, 2 points for survival) and the plausible ranges (for example fork length 300-1000 mm) were chosen for this document.

Inputs used for the checks

The FY2025 Production Harvest workbook is read here for two cross-checks (pond grow-out, and the September 2025 harvest). One row per pond cycle, sheets FALL 2024, Spring 2025 and Fall 2025:

ph_path <- here::here("data-raw/hatchery-resources/FY2025 Supporting Excel Tables/FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx")

extract_col <- function(raw, pattern) {
  matched <- names(raw)[str_detect(str_squish(names(raw)), regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))]
  if (length(matched) == 0) return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(raw)))
  if (length(matched) == 1) return(raw[[matched]])
  exec(coalesce, !!!as.list(raw[matched]))
}
excel_date <- function(x) as.Date(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)), origin = "1899-12-30")

production_harvest_fy2025 <- map2(c("FALL 2024", "Spring 2025", "Fall 2025"), c("Fall 2024", "Spring 2025", "Fall 2025"), \(sheet, season) {
  raw <- readxl::read_excel(ph_path, sheet = sheet, col_types = "text")
  tibble(pond = extract_col(raw, "^Pond$"),
         stocked_date = excel_date(extract_col(raw, "^Stocked? Date$")),
         start_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^Start #$"))),
         harvest_date = excel_date(extract_col(raw, "^Harvest Date$")),
         end_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^End # Live$|^End #$"))),
         survival_percent = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^Survival$")))) |>
    filter(!is.na(pond), pond != "Pond") |>
    mutate(season = season, pond = str_to_upper(pond),
           # some seasons record survival as a fraction (0-1)
           survival_percent = if (!all(is.na(survival_percent)) && max(survival_percent, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1) survival_percent * 100 else survival_percent)
}) |> list_rbind()

Age / facility lookup

KFNFH_age_facility_lookup maps each pond or net pen to the age class(es) of the fish held there, by fiscal year. It is the single source of fish age: KFNFH_pond_growout and KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly take age_class and starting_count from it. age_class holds classes such as "1/2" or "wild", not a single age.

How the lookup is built

The lookup is built from the workbooks and reports only:

  • Net pens (UKL and Gerber): nphistory.xlsx. Age is the operation year minus the capture year; starting_count is the number of fish stocked.
  • Ponds (A, B, C and P series): every pond cycle in the Production Harvest workbooks and the annual report tables. A cycle counts in the fiscal year it was stocked and in the fiscal year it was harvested. The age class is that fiscal year minus the lot’s collection year (4 means 4 or older); East Side Springs and mixed lots are other, wild and salvage lots are wild. starting_count is the number of fish at the start of the first cycle harvested in the year.

Facility-years that no cycle or net pen record covers have no row (for example the FY2020 ponds).

KFNFH_historical_collection_release is built from Table 1 and Table 7 of the FY2025 report, which repeat the full history (FY2016-2025) with updated numbers; the broodstock columns come from the report text.

FY2024 larvae_collected is 30,142 in FY2025 Table 1, but 30,150 in the FY2024 report (Tables 1 and 4, and the narrative), in FY2025 Table 7 of the FY2025 report itself, and in the hatchery’s own workbook (the cumulative “Total Collected To Date” in 2024 Larval Collection and Early Rearing Summary Data.xlsx ends at 30,150). Three sources agree on 30,150, so the object uses the Table 7 value (30,150) for all years (it equals Table 1 in every other year). The same workbooks also confirm FY2023 (6,036) and FY2025 (70,049).

Pond grow-out

KFNFH_pond_growout combines the pond tables of the FY2021-FY2025 reports. The Production Harvest Data Sheet workbooks describe the same pond cycles; for FY2021-2024 their rows match the report rows on pond and harvest date (start numbers are identical; end numbers and survival agree for about 95% of rows), so they are not appended as a second copy. The script:

  1. keeps the report tables as the primary source (they have the full set of columns, including weights);
  2. adds FY2025 from the FY2025 report pond tables (Tables 10-12) so FY2025 has the same columns as earlier years;
  3. validates the FY2025 rows against the workbook, and would append (flagged source = "production_harvest_workbook") any workbook row that is not in the report tables (there are none);
  4. replaces a cycle reported as still in progress (no harvest date) in an earlier report with the later, completed record of the same pond and stocking date;
  5. removes a completed cycle that is listed in two consecutive reports (44 cycles: 24 in both FY2023 Table 7 and FY2024 Table 6, and 20 in both the FY2022 tables and FY2023 Table 5), keeping the later report’s row;
  6. takes age_class and starting_count from the lookup.

Validation of the completed FY2025 cycles against the Production Harvest workbook:

key <- function(d, stock, pond = "pond") ifelse(is.na(d[[stock]]), NA, paste(d[[pond]], d[[stock]]))

pond_2025_report <- KFNFH_pond_growout |> filter(fiscal_year == 2025, source == "annual_report_table")

fy25_check <- pond_2025_report |>
  filter(!is.na(harvest_date)) |>
  mutate(k = key(pick(everything()), "pond_stock_date")) |>
  inner_join(production_harvest_fy2025 |> filter(!is.na(harvest_date)) |>
               mutate(k = key(pick(everything()), "stocked_date")) |>
               select(k, wb_start = start_number, wb_end = end_number, wb_survival = survival_percent),
             by = "k")

tibble(completed_report_rows_fy25 = sum(!is.na(pond_2025_report$harvest_date)),
       matched_to_workbook = nrow(fy25_check),
       start_number_equal = mean(fy25_check$start_number == fy25_check$wb_start, na.rm = TRUE),
       end_number_equal = mean(fy25_check$end_number == fy25_check$wb_end, na.rm = TRUE),
       end_number_minus_morts_equal = mean(fy25_check$end_number - fy25_check$harvest_mortality_number == fy25_check$wb_end, na.rm = TRUE),
       survival_within_0.5 = mean(abs(fy25_check$survival_percent - fy25_check$wb_survival) < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE))
completed_report_rows_fy25 matched_to_workbook start_number_equal end_number_equal end_number_minus_morts_equal survival_within_0.5
55 55 1 0.436 1 1

For the completed FY2025 cycles, start numbers are identical and survival agrees. The FY2025 report’s End # counts fish before harvest mortalities, while the workbook’s End # is the live count, so end_number - harvest_mortality_number equals the workbook value for every matched row.

Incubation and hatch results

KFNFH_LRS_ESS_incubation_hatch (the _2024 suffix is dropped) holds the wild East Side Springs LRS spawning crosses of FY2024 (report Table 3) and FY2025 (the ESS metadata workbook, identical to report Table 3), with the family-group count and, for FY2025, the second fry count.

  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(), collected = sum(collected),
            collected_excl_restock = sum(collected[!restock]),
            stocked = sum(stocked),
            survival = round(100 * stocked / collected, 1))
fiscal_year rows collected collected_excl_restock stocked survival
2023 14 6037 NA 3969 65.7
2024 25 37477 NA 27736 74.0
2025 15 70049 NA 65847 94.0

restock flags rows whose culture unit is a “Restock” (larvae moved back into a tank that was already stocked). In FY2024 the five restock rows add up to 7,327 fish, which is exactly the difference between the sum of the collected column (37,477) and the 30,150 larvae actually collected; so sum collected only over non-restock rows (or use KFNFH_historical_collection_release$larvae_collected) for collection totals. In FY2025 the rows sum to the reported 70,049, which is also the cumulative collected total in the hatchery workbook, so those restock rows are fish collected that day, not re-counts.

date_raw keeps the date text as reported because FY2025 (and some FY2023) entries span two days ("5/8/2025 & 5/9/2025"). date is the first date.

Totals in the reports for comparison: FY2023 6,036 collected and 3,969 stocked (65.8%); FY2025 70,049 collected and 65,847 stocked (94.0%). The FY2023 rows sum to 6,037 collected (the report’s total row says 6,036), a one-fish difference inside the report.

Mortality events (from the report narratives)

Events E01-E28 come from the FY2021-2024 report narratives. Identifying an event and describing it (period, location, category, cause, affected population, the loss as reported, the confidence class) is a reading of the report narratives and cannot be taken from a table. Those text columns are the only values taken from the hand-compiled mortality_events.csv. Everything that can be checked against the reports or workbooks is computed in process-hatchery-data.R. Events E29-E37 come from the FY2025 report and are built there too, with their losses taken from the FY2025 water quality and mortality workbook (daily sheets and Sheet1).

  • every event is tied to a phrase in the report that describes it (the script stops if a phrase is missing);
  • percent_lost and n_mortality are recomputed from the net pen records (nphistory.xlsx), the larval rearing tables and workbook, and numbers in the report text;
  • severity_tier is recomputed from percent_lost with a fixed rule (over 70% Catastrophic, 30-70% Major, 10-30% Moderate, under 10% Minor; no loss in a non-mortality event is a near-miss; no number is qualitative only).

FY2025 events (E29-E37)

The FY2025 report (FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf) describes the summer 2025 mortality spike and other losses that are not in the FY2021-2024 event list. The losses come from KFNFH_WQ_FY2025_2 (version 1).xlsx: the daily pond sheets (OctobertoDecember_WQ, JantoMar_WQ, AprtoJun_WQ, JulytoSept_WQ), which have a Morts column, a lot column (CY) and a Comments column, and Sheet1, which gives the fish at the start and at harvest of the ponds harvested early in September 2025. Where the workbooks do not give a loss, the number in the report text or Table 8 is used. As for the earlier events, each event is tied to a phrase in the report (the chunk stops if a phrase is missing), the severity tier comes from the fixed rule, and an event with no percent loss is “Qualitative only” even when the report gives a number of fish. The events are built in process-hatchery-data.R (section FINAL OBJECTS, Mortality events); the FY2025 events are the rows E29 to E37:

KFNFH_mortality_events |>
  filter(event_id >= "E29") |>
  select(event_id, year, period, category, percent_lost, loss_as_reported, severity_tier, loss_source)
event_id year period category percent_lost loss_as_reported severity_tier loss_source

E33 2025 25 Oct 2024 to 03 Mar 2025 (pond cycle) disease 30.2 Survival just under 70% (workbook: 69.8%) Major (30-70% loss) FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx, sheet Spring 2025 (pond P10)
E34 2025 03 to 18 July 2025 water_quality 1.2 274 dead fish recorded in the daily log over 16 days (more were logged as unretrievable). The report only describes ‘a minor acute mortality event’ with 11 dead fish on one morning with DO below 2 mg/L; the pond had good survival for the season Minor (<10% loss) KFNFH_WQ_FY2025_2 (version 1).xlsx, sheet JulytoSept_WQ (Morts, Comments) and FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx, sheet Fall 2025 (start number)
E35 2025 08 May 2025 to 12 Jun 2025 (larval collections into the tanks) disease 5.1 3,562 observed fry deaths = 5.1% of the stock (the report text says 3,652; Table 8 and its total row say 3,562) Minor (<10% loss) FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf, Table 8 (total row)
E36 2025 08 May 2025 to 12 Jun 2025 (larval collections into the tanks) other 0.9 Unobserved mortality = 0.9% of the stock, ‘much lower than in years past’ Minor (<10% loss) FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf, Table 8 (total row)
E37 2025 Spring 2025 (weeks after hatch) other NA ‘Nearly total losses of the LRS fry within several weeks post hatch’; no number is given Qualitative only (unquantified) FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf (text)

Notes on how these events were built:

  • E29 is the ESS2025 lot in ponds C1 and C2. Loss is from Sheet1: fish at the start minus (harvested + harvest-day deaths), which is the same definition as the Survival column of that sheet. The daily logs record fewer dead fish than were lost, because fish that could not be retrieved are not counted (the comments note them every day).
  • E34 differs from the report. The report calls it a minor event with 11 dead fish on one morning; the daily log for pond C6 shows deaths on every day from 3 to 18 July, with the staff logging bottom dissolved oxygen of 0.2-0.6 mg/L. The event is built from the workbook (the Excel file wins), and the report phrase is kept as its citation.
  • E35 uses Table 8 (3,562 deaths, 5.1% of 70,049); the report text says 3,652, which is a transposition because 3,562 is both the table total and 5.1%.
  • E30, E32 and E37 have numbers of dead fish (or none) but no number at risk in the reports or workbooks, so they have no percent and are qualitative.

Sheet1 and the Production Harvest workbook do not agree on the ponds harvested early. Sheet1 (used above) gives fewer harvested fish than the Fall 2025 sheet of FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx:

harvest_2025 <- readxl::read_excel(
  here::here("data-raw/hatchery-resources/FY2025 Supporting Excel Tables/KFNFH_WQ_FY2025_2 (version 1).xlsx"),
  sheet = "Sheet1") |>
  set_names(c("pond", "harvest_date", "initial", "harvested", "harvest_morts", "survival")) |>
  filter(!is.na(initial))
harvest_2025 |>
  select(pond, harvest_date, initial, harvested_sheet1 = harvested, harvest_morts_sheet1 = harvest_morts, survival_sheet1 = survival) |>
  left_join(production_harvest_fy2025 |>
              filter(season == "Fall 2025") |>
              select(pond, start_number, end_number_production_harvest = end_number, survival_percent_production_harvest = survival_percent),
            by = "pond") |>
  mutate(difference_in_harvested = end_number_production_harvest - harvested_sheet1)
pond harvest_date initial harvested_sheet1 harvest_morts_sheet1 survival_sheet1 start_number end_number_production_harvest survival_percent_production_harvest difference_in_harvested
C1 2025-09-11 25530 9883 1438 0.443 25530 11553 49.734 1670
C2 2025-09-10 25009 9622 2661 0.491 25009 10702 48.507 1080
B3 2025-09-29 7923 4860 111 0.627 7923 4860 62.741 0

The differences (1,670 fish for C1 and 1,080 for C2) are not the harvest-day deaths in Sheet1, so they are not explained by that column. Sheet1 is used for E29; the other workbook is shown for comparison.

Sources of the losses

Each event is tied to the phrase of the report that describes it (report_phrase, in the report of report_year), and its loss to the workbook, table or text in loss_source. The script stops if a phrase is not in the report, so an event cannot be mis-cited. Event E07 (Gerber net pen emergency harvest, 2021) has no percent_lost because the report states no loss, so its tier is “Non-mortality”. Event E22 (August 2024 dissolved-oxygen crashes in ponds P12 and P13) has no percent_lost: the FY2024 report only says “the acute loss of several thousand fish between both instances, as well as some chronic losses”, and the pond records cannot be turned into a combined loss (P13’s May 2024 stocking of 3,012 fish was split before harvest), so its tier is “Qualitative only (unquantified)”.

Monthly pond mortality (from the mortality spreadsheets)

Age and starting count come from the lookup so all objects use the same age definition. The FY2024 workbook covers 1 January to 22 September 2024 only (the October to December 2023 quarter and the last week of September 2024 are missing), so FY2024 totals are a partial year. The P-series pond matrices in the FALL 2023 MORTALITY and SPRING 2024 MORTALITY sheets of the Production Harvest Data Sheet workbooks cover November and December 2023 and could fill part of that gap.

Pond counts and acreage are read from the facility description of each report. Indoor tank gallons are summed from the tank lists in the reports: the FY2022-FY2024 reports list only the greenhouse tanks (the second indoor building is first described in the FY2025 report), so each year has the value its report supports: 10,360 (FY2021), 12,035 (FY2022), 12,755 (FY2023 and FY2024), 16,395 (FY2025). The planned build-out has no gallons in any report (NA).

QC checks and plots

One subsection per data object. Each has a table of checks (rows_failing is the number of rows that break the check; status is pass or FLAG, and every flag has a note saying what it is) followed by plots. A flag is a property of the reports or workbooks that the package reproduces, or a documented limitation; it is not corrected in the object. Each subsection ends with a table of missing values (NA) for every variable of the object. The flags are collected in the QC summary at the end of this section.

library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

qc_all <- tibble()
qc <- function(object, check, failed, note = "") {
  n_fail <- sum(failed, na.rm = TRUE)
  qc_all <<- bind_rows(qc_all, tibble(object = object, check = check, rows_checked = sum(!is.na(failed)),
                                      rows_failing = n_fail, status = if (n_fail == 0) "pass" else "FLAG",
                                      note = if (n_fail == 0) "" else note))
  invisible(failed)
}
# tables are written as HTML tables with wrapped text and fixed column widths (see the style block above), so they fit the page
qc_table <- function(o) {
  x <- qc_all |> filter(object %in% o)
  if (length(o) == 1) {
    x |> select(check, checked = rows_checked, failing = rows_failing, status, note) |>
      knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="qc-table"')
  } else {
    x |> select(object, check, checked = rows_checked, failing = rows_failing, status, note) |>
      knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="qc-flags"')
  }
}

# missing values of every variable of an object, as a compact HTML table
na_summary <- function(x) {
  tibble(variable = names(x),
         type = map_chr(x, \(v) class(v)[1]),
         missing = map_int(x, \(v) sum(is.na(v))),
         pct_missing = round(100 * missing / nrow(x), 1),
         rows = nrow(x)) |>
    knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="na-table"')
}

fy_start <- function(fy) as.Date(paste0(fy - 1, "-10-01"))
fy_end <- function(fy) as.Date(paste0(fy, "-09-30"))
fiscal_year_of <- function(d) year(d) + if_else(month(d) >= 10, 1, 0)

KFNFH_mortality_events and KFNFH_mortality_events_summary

ev <- KFNFH_mortality_events
s <- KFNFH_mortality_events_summary
o <- "KFNFH_mortality_events"
tier_rule <- case_when(
  !ev$mortality_event & !is.na(ev$percent_lost) & ev$percent_lost == 0 ~ "Near-miss (no mortality observed)",
  !ev$mortality_event ~ "Non-mortality (escape/collection/reproductive)",
  is.na(ev$percent_lost) ~ "Qualitative only (unquantified)",
  ev$percent_lost > 70 ~ "Catastrophic (>70% loss)",
  ev$percent_lost >= 30 ~ "Major (30-70% loss)",
  ev$percent_lost >= 10 ~ "Moderate (10-30% loss)",
  TRUE ~ "Minor (<10% loss)")
qc(o, "one row per event_id", duplicated(ev$event_id))
qc(o, "percent_lost between 0 and 100", ev$percent_lost < 0 | ev$percent_lost > 100)
qc(o, "severity_tier follows percent_lost", ev$severity_tier != tier_rule)
qc(o, "report_phrase present", is.na(ev$report_phrase))
qc(o, "loss_source present when percent_lost present", !is.na(ev$percent_lost) & is.na(ev$loss_source))
qc(o, "event year 2019-2025 and not after its report", ev$year < 2019 | ev$year > ev$report_year)
qc(o, "category is one of the six categories", !(ev$category %in% c("disease", "water_quality", "weather", "predation", "equipment", "other")))
o2 <- "KFNFH_mortality_events_summary"
qc(o2, "same events, in the same order, as KFNFH_mortality_events", s$event_id != ev$event_id)
qc(o2, "percent_mortality = percent_lost", abs(coalesce(s$percent_mortality, -1) - coalesce(ev$percent_lost, -1)) > 0.05)
qc(o2, "n_mortality >= 0", s$n_mortality < 0)
qc_table(c(o, o2))

KFNFH_pond_growout growth_mm_day within 0.1 of (end_tl_mm - start_tl_mm) / days 4 251 FY2023 Table 7 (and 3 FY2024 Table 7 rows): the reported ‘mm/day’ equals the length change divided by 30, i.e. mm per 30 days
KFNFH_pond_growout age_class present 11 359 ponds missing from the age lookup
KFNFH_pond_growout fiscal_year = fiscal year of the harvest date 41 359 fiscal_year is the year of the report that lists the cycle; reports also list cycles harvested just before or after their fiscal year
KFNFH_age_facility_lookup every facility-year of KFNFH_pond_growout (A, B, C, P series) is in the lookup 2 359 cycles are listed in the lookup for the fiscal year they were stocked and harvested; a cycle listed under the report year may fall in a neighbouring year
KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly one pond record per pond, month and fiscal year 1070 1516 FY2024 and FY2025 are daily log rows labelled with their month (the FY2023 sheet is one value per pond and month); sum by month before using as monthly counts

One age definition everywhere

Every object with a pond or facility now takes age_class and starting_count from the lookup:

bind_rows(
  KFNFH_pond_growout |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_pond_growout", fiscal_year, matched = !is.na(age_class)),
  KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly", fiscal_year, matched = !is.na(age_class))) |>
  group_by(object, fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(), with_age = sum(matched), share = round(with_age / rows, 2), .groups = "drop")

The lookup starts in FY2019 and is sparse before FY2021, so FY2021 and FY2022 have the lowest coverage. Filling those is listed under remaining gaps.

Description of each data object

All values come from the annual reports (PDF) or the hatchery workbooks (Excel).

Draft data dictionary

One row per column of each data object, with its type, a description and the source of its values. The descriptions are the ones in R/data.R (they are parsed from the roxygen blocks, so editing them there updates this table). The source is a PDF title, or a workbook and sheet name; a column whose source differs from the rest of its object has its own entry. This is a draft: columns that are not described in R/data.R show as “TODO”, and the table is also written to data-raw/hatchery_data_dictionary.csv.

pdf_2021 <- "20240912_FY2021_KFNFH_Annual_Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2022 <- "20240830_FY2022 KFNFH Annual Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2023 <- "20240801_FY2023 KFNFH Annual Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2024 <- "20250619_FY2024 KFNFH Annual Report_Final Draft.pdf"
pdf_2025 <- "FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf"

dictionary_objects <- final_objects
get_object <- function(name) get(name)

# descriptions: \item \code{column}: text lines of each roxygen block in R/data.R
parse_data_r <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path)
  starts <- which(str_detect(lines, "^#' @name "))
  map2(starts, c(starts[-1] - 1, length(lines)), function(from, to) {
    block <- lines[from:to]
    items <- block[str_detect(block, "^#'\\s+\\\\item \\\\code\\{")]
    tibble(object = str_trim(str_remove(lines[from], "^#' @name ")),
           column = str_trim(str_match(items, "\\\\code\\{([^}]+)\\}")[, 2]),
           description = items |>
             str_remove("^#'\\s+\\\\item \\\\code\\{[^}]+\\}:?\\s*") |>
             str_replace_all("\\\\code\\{([^}]*)\\}", "`\\1`") |>
             str_replace_all("\\\\%", "%") |>
             str_squish())
  }) |> list_rbind()
}
documented <- parse_data_r(here::here("R/data.R"))

data_dictionary <- map(dictionary_objects, function(o) {
  x <- get_object(o)
  tibble(object = o, column = names(x), type = map_chr(x, \(v) class(v)[1]))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(documented, by = c("object", "column")) |>
  left_join(source_default, by = "object") |>
  left_join(source_overrides |> filter(object != "*") |> rename(source_override = source), by = c("object", "column")) |>
  left_join(source_overrides |> filter(object == "*") |> select(column, source_all = source), by = "column") |>
  transmute(object, column, type,
            description = coalesce(description, "TODO: not described in R/data.R"),
            data_source = coalesce(source_override, source_all, source))

write_csv(data_dictionary, here::here("data-raw", "hatchery_data_dictionary.csv"))

# described in R/data.R but not a column of the object, and columns with no description
documented |>

  anti_join(data_dictionary, by = c("object", "column"))

Remaining gaps

Gap Why it is still open Next step
Early rearing FY2021 and FY2022 The FY2021 and FY2022 reports have no culture-unit table Ask USFWS for the larval tank records for those years
FY2022 pond tables 3-4 Embedded as images and OCR’d earlier; inventory_source is NA for those rows Re-check against the source images
FY2021 pond PIT tag study (Tables 5-7) and FY2022 historical PIT detections (Table 6) Different table types, never imported Decide if the model needs them
Weight gain and feed conversion FY2025 start and end weights are now in KFNFH_pond_growout (from the report tables), but weight gain is not reported for FY2025 (left NA), and feed conversion is not extracted for any year Compute weight gain from the start and end weights if needed; extract feed conversion from the workbooks (not in the repository)
Mortality events E29-E37 (FY2025) Added from the FY2025 report, the WQ workbook and Sheet1. E30, E32 and E37 have no number at risk, and Sheet1 and the Production Harvest workbook disagree on the C1/C2 harvest Ask USFWS which harvest count is right and for the number of fish in the tanks after the September harvest
Mortality spreadsheets FY2024 Oct-Dec 2023 Quarter not found Ask USFWS
Age lookup: FY2020 ponds (A1, A2, P5, P11-P15), unoperated FY2025 pens, extra age classes Not in the reports or workbooks Ask USFWS for the facility-by-age records
Magnitudes for qualitative mortality events (including E22) Most events have no number in the reports or workbooks Ask USFWS or agree how to assign severity numerically

Notes for the model

  • KFNFH_pond_growout is the stage-specific growth and survival table (mm/day, survival percent, by pond and season, FY2021-2025).
  • KFNFH_mortality_events and KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly give event frequency/severity and routine mortality.
  • KFNFH_capacity bounds production; KFNFH_historical_collection_release and KFNFH_hatchery_release give inputs and outputs by year.
  • age_class has multi-age values ("1/2/3") where a facility held several age groups in one year. Decide how to allocate mortality and growth in those cases before using it as a stage.
